# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 ☝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 ✌]

I need to establish a communication protocol with Mute, since gestures are the only way Mute can send me information, and speech is the only way I can send Blind information (Blind can't see gestures, and I can't hear Mute's speech).

Let me think about what Mute is trying to tell me. Mute gestured 👍☝ and 👎✌. This looks like Mute is trying to establish a code: maybe 👍 = correct/yes paired with a number (☝=1), and 👎 = wrong/no paired with a number (✌=2). This could mean "wire 1 is correct/safe" and "wire 2 is wrong/bad" — or it could be Mute asking me questions, but Mute can't hear my speech reply directly... wait, actually Mute CAN hear (Mute just can't speak or touch). So Mute hears my speech.

So the plan: Mute reads the manual and gestures clues to me. I see the bomb. I need to combine my visual info with Mute's manual clues, then speak instructions to Blind (who can hear me) to act.

I should report what I see to Mute (via speech, since Mute can hear) and to Blind, and ask Mute to clarify the gesture meaning.

```
speak(to="mute", text="I see: display shows 0, light is blue, three wires - wire 1 red, wire 2 yellow, wire 3 blue. I received your gestures but need a clearer code. Please gesture a number alone to indicate which wire is safe to cut, or thumbs up after a wire number to confirm, thumbs down to reject. Confirm: do your gestures thumbs-up-one and thumbs-down-two mean wire 1 is safe and wire 2 is dangerous?")
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [orange]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]

The light changed from blue to orange - this is important new information I need to relay. Mute is gesturing again: 👎, ☝, 👎 as three separate gestures this turn. This could be answering my question sequentially, or it could be new independent signals.

Let me interpret cautiously: perhaps 👎 = "no/wrong", ☝ = "one" (wire 1), 👎 = "no/wrong" again. This might mean "not wire 1" is wrong interpretation... or Mute is listing wire statuses: wire1=👎(bad), and then ☝ points to something, 👎 again.

Since I can't be sure, I should tell Mute exactly what changed (light color changed to orange, display still 0), and ask Mute to use a clearer numbered protocol: gesture the wire number, then thumbs up/down for that specific wire, one pair at a time, waiting for my confirmation between each.

I also should relay to Blind that nothing should be touched yet - we're still establishing communication.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Update: display 0, light changed from blue to orange, wires unchanged - 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. I could not parse your three separate gestures. Please slow down: send one wire number, then immediately one thumbs up or thumbs down for only that wire, in the same turn, like this order: wire-number then verdict. Repeat for each wire across turns. I will confirm receipt each time before you continue.")
speak(to="blind", text="We are still figuring out the code between me and Mute. Do not touch any wire yet. Wait for my instruction.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ 👍]

The light keeps changing each turn (blue → orange → yellow) with display staying at 0 and wires unchanged. This cycling light might just be ambient/cosmetic, or it might be counting down/cycling in a pattern that matters. I should keep reporting it.

Mute now gestured ✌👍 (two, thumbs up) in one turn — following my requested format of wire-number then verdict. This suggests wire 2 = thumbs up = safe/correct!

Let me confirm this reading back to Mute and also give Blind a heads-up, but I want to be careful not to instruct Blind to cut yet until I get full confirmation, since a wrong action detonates the bomb. Let me ask Mute to also verify wire 1 and wire 3 status to be thorough, and confirm my understanding of the ✌👍 pairing.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Received: two, thumbs-up together - I read this as wire 2 is safe. Light now cycling colors each turn - blue, then orange, then yellow, display still 0. Please confirm wire 2 is the one to cut by repeating two, thumbs-up once more. Then tell me about wire 1 and wire 3 the same way, one pair per turn, so I am certain before Blind touches anything.")
speak(to="blind", text="Do not act yet. We believe wire 2 yellow may be safe but I need confirmation from Mute first. Stand by.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ 👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟 👎]

Mute confirmed: ✌👍 (wire 2 = safe/good), then ☝👎 (wire 1 = bad), then 🤟👎 (wire 3 = bad, using 🤟 for "three" perhaps, or a different gesture for 3 - could be ✊ or 🤟 as an alternate "three" sign). This is consistent and clear now: wire 2 is the correct one to cut, wires 1 and 3 are dangerous.

The light is now red, which could be significant (danger indicator?) but display remains 0. I should relay this final light state to Mute in case it matters to the manual instructions, but I think we have enough confirmation to proceed. Let me instruct Blind to cut wire 2 only, being very explicit and clear, and warn against touching wires 1 and 3.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Confirmed and understood: wire 2 safe, wire 1 bad, wire 3 bad. Light is now red, display still 0. I will instruct Blind to cut wire 2 only. Please gesture stop immediately with a fist if this is wrong before Blind acts.")
speak(to="blind", text="Instruction: cut wire 2 only - the yellow wire. Do not touch wire 1 or wire 3. Wire 2 the yellow one is confirmed safe by the manual. Proceed only with wire 2.")
wait()
```
